{{Short description|Mathematical concept}}
[[File:Median triangle.svg|thumb|upright=1.3|
Reference triangle: {{math|△''ABC''}} <br/>
{{legend-line|solid red 2px|Median triangle: {{math|△''BGF''}}|inline=yes}} <br/>
Median triangle of {{math|△''BGF''}}: {{math|△''BKH''}}<br/>
[[Similarity (geometry)|Similarity]]: {{math|△''BGF'' ~ △''BKH''}}]]

In [[geometry]], the '''median triangle''' of a given (reference) triangle is a [[triangle]], the sides of which are equal and parallel to the [[Median (geometry)|medians]] of its reference triangle. The [[Area of a triangle|area]] of the median triangle is 3/4 of the area of its reference triangle:

<math display=block>| \triangle BGF| = \frac{3}{4} |\triangle ABC|</math>

The median triangle of the median triangle is similar to the reference triangle of the first median triangle with a [[scaling factor]] of 3/4:<ref>Roger A. Johnson: ''Advanced Euclidean Geometry''. Dover 2007, {{ISBN|978-0-486-46237-0}}, pp.&nbsp;282–283</ref><ref>Claudi Alsina, Roger B. Nelsen: ''Charming Proofs: A Journey Into Elegant Mathematics''. MAA, 2010, {{ISBN|9780883853481}}, p.&nbsp;165</ref><ref>Árpad Bényi, Branko Ćurgus: "Outer Median Triangles". In: ''Mathematics Magazine'', Vol. 87, No. 3 (June 2014), pp.&nbsp;185–194 ([https://www.jstor.org/stable/pdf/10.4169/math.mag.87.3.185.pdf JSTOR])</ref>

<math display=block>\frac{|BH|}{|BC|} = \frac{|HK|}{|AB|} = \frac{|BK|}{|AC|} = \frac{3}{4}</math>
